records.question: is red meat linked to colorectal cancer
records.answer: Yes, red meat is linked to colorectal cancer [1]. The risk of colorectal cancer increases approximately linearly with increasing intake of red and processed meats up to approximately 140 g/day [2]. High intake of red and processed meat is associated with a significant increased risk of colorectal, colon, and rectal cancers [2].

records.question: does coffee consumption affect liver disease
records.answer: [1] Drinking coffee may have benefits for the liver, irrespective of whether coffee was boiled or filtered [1]. Inverse associations between coffee consumption and liver disease were observed, including reduced risk of mortality from chronic liver disease (RR=0.55, 95% CI: 0.48–0.63; P-trend<0.0001) [1]. Similar associations were found in various subgroups, including those without diabetes, HBV- and HCV-negative cases, and in analyses stratified by age, body mass index, alcohol and smoking dose [1].

records.question: is there a link between dairy and prostate cancer
records.answer: Yes, several studies suggest a link between dairy consumption and increased risk of prostate cancer. [1] states that "The results from this large prospective study suggest that intake of calcium or some related component contained in dairy foods is associated with increased prostate cancer risk." [2] also mentions a "potent link" between dairy intake and prostate cancer, suggesting that insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1) and steroid hormones present in milk may be contributing factors. [3] found a strong correlation between milk consumption and prostate cancer mortality, with a correlation coefficient of 0.766. [4] proposes that high dairy consumption may lead to increased mTORC1 signaling, which may have adverse effects on prostate health. [5] conducted a meta-analysis of case-control studies and found a combined odds ratio of 1.68 between milk consumption and prostate cancer.
